explanation: An autosomal recessive pedigree traces the inheritance of a recessive trait on an autosome. In such pedigrees, the disease can skip generations, and two unaffected heterozygous parents (carriers) can have an affected offspring (aa).

questions.q: Which of the following is a classic feature of an autosomal recessive pedigree?
opts: The trait appears in every single generation without fail.
Affected individuals must always have two affected parents.
Unaffected parents can have an affected child if both parents are carriers.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because if a disease is autosomal recessive, two carrier parents (Aa x Aa) are phenotypically unaffected but have a 25% chance of producing an affected (aa) child.
